# Harmonic for Hacker News Harmonic for Hacker News is an Android Hacker News client which is meant to be modern, fast and well thought out. You can find it on Google Play for download. This has been my personal side project since 2020 and since starting my PhD in 2021 the time I have to dedicate to Harmonic has decreased. My personal philosophy on side projects is that the most important thing is building something that is actually shipped. Since much of my knowledge on building Android apps is ~10 years old, Harmonic does not use Kotlin or the latest Android API's and is probably not the easiest app to dig into the source code of. However, it is shipped, and it works fairly well in my opinion at least. :) The purpose of open-sourcing Harmonic is thus mainly to enable interested users to submit pull requests fixing issues or adding features. I would like to still be able to find my way around the app's code so I am not looking for a full Kotlin rewrite but if you want to make the app work better with foldables, fix a typo or add support for Android 13's themed icons all that would be much appreciated. I'll still commit things myself when I have time. # Features * Basic account functionality: log in, vote, comment, and submit * Dark theme * Browser choice: integrated or system browser * Key word filtering of stories * Option of "clearing clicked stories" to hide stories you've seen * Ability to export bookmarks to a text file

steps.reasoning_content:
Good. The other dialogs use "Done" or "Dismiss" as the negative button, which is correct per Material Design — those are the cancel/close actions and belong on the left. 

The only problematic dialog is the "Discard comment?" / "Discard post?" dialog in `ComposeActivity.java`. The fix is:
1. Swap "Discard" to be the positive button (right side)
2. Swap "Cancel" to be the negative button (left side)

But wait — there's a subtlety. The "Discard" button has an onClick listener that calls `finish()`, while "Cancel" has `null`. After swapping:
- `setPositiveButton("Discard", listener)` — Discard goes on the right with the finish logic


- `setNegativeButton("Cancel", null)` — Cancel goes on the left with no listener (the default behavior handles dismissing the dialog)

This aligns with Material Design principles, where destructive actions like "Discard" are positioned on the right as the affirmative action, and "Cancel" stays on the left as the negative action.

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `setNegativeButton("Discard", ...)` | `setPositiveButton("Discard", ...)` |

**Other dialogs checked:** No other dialogs have this issue — the "Done"/"Dismiss" buttons in `MainActivity.java` and `UserActions.java` correctly use `setNegativeButton`, as they represent the cancel/close action.
